My family has worked this land in Quzhou for generations. I know what this soil wants and what it will give back. I am 73 now, my knees ache in the cold, so I hire the village machinery station to do the deep work — ploughing, seeding, harvesting. I pay the fee like everyone else on the street.

Here in Quzhou, you grow wheat in winter and corn in summer. That is the only sensible thing. The government water well is nearby, and I know exactly how many times I need to pump to get a good crop. I have done this for fifty years.

For wheat, I will plant Jimai 22 again — same as last three years. It does not give me surprises. I buy compound fertilizer from the co-op for base application when I plant, then top-dress with urea in April when the wheat starts to stretch upward. I water four times: before the ground freezes, at jointing, at heading, and once more when the grain is filling if it stays dry. I spray herbicide in November when the little weeds first show, then spray again at heading time for rust and aphids — that is when everyone on my road sprays, so I spray too.

For corn, I will plant hybrid seeds from the township supply station. My son helps me plant when he comes home in June after the wheat is off the field. I put fertilizer down at planting and then again when the corn is knee-high. I water once or twice depending on rain. I spray once for the stem borer, maybe twice if I see more damage than usual.

I farm 8 mu. All wheat in winter, all corn in summer on the same land.
